title: Draft color selection is non-deterministic (missing HashMap tie-break)
release_pin_note: latest stable release per GitHub API 2026-10-19T23:41Z; == pinned release dir (pinned 2026-10-19, minisign-verified v0.114.0)

scenario: verbatim re-run of the verified v0.113.0 harness: find_best_colors/dominant_colors copied verbatim from release sources; tied pool (one card each W/U/B/R/G, constant score 1.0); 30 separate OS processes
result: find_best_colors: 14 distinct top-2 orderings across 30 processes (score-only sort, no tie-break — HashMap iteration order leaks). dominant_colors: B,G in all 30 runs. Fixed control: B,G in all 30 runs. Defect persists unchanged since v0.103.0; v0.114.0 sources byte-identical to v0.113.0.
limitations: Browser/UI 'Suggest deck' click path not exercised; the helper function it calls is exercised verbatim from the release sources.
Real score_card gives per-card quality scores; constant score reproduces the reported tie condition only.
No engine game states apply to a deckbuilder report (per playbook deckbuilder rule).
Rust HashMap (RandomState) iteration order is per-process; 30 processes is the established sample for this issue.
